claude.rationale: gap_45 = 1: minority economic interests in the operating wind-farm project companies (the customer-facing generation asset, T4) crossed to PSP/Vertuous at closing via the three PSAs, but the operating and administrative processes (T5) were NOT transferred to the co-investor — they were retained by the Company and provided back under the Sponsor Services Agreement dated June 16, 2017, a documented product-vs-process split at closing that was contractually absorbed (gap_mitigated = yes). gap_56 = 0: because T5 processes did not move to the co-investor and personnel remained governed within the existing Pattern organization under the A&R Multilateral Management Services Agreement, there is no closing-structure mismatch of processes transferring without their people. This is coded as a minority co-investment where controlling intent stays with the Company (T1 continue), so no Tier-1 fusion is documented.

gemini.rationale: The slice documents that PSP Investments acquired minority economic interests in specific wind-farm project companies (T4), but the operating and administrative processes (T5) were retained by the Company, resulting in a gap_45. This gap was mitigated by a Sponsor Services Agreement. Management and personnel (T6) also remained with the Company, aligning with the retained processes, so gap_56 is 0.

openai.rationale: PSP acquired minority economic interests in three specific wind-farm project companies, while Pattern retained majority ownership and continued operating and administering the projects. Thus, customer-facing generation assets crossed the ownership boundary without the associated processes transferring to PSP, creating a documented T4–T5 gap. The Sponsor Services Agreement and the A&R Multilateral Management Services Agreement contractually bridged that gap through administration, management services, and employee arrangements, while the existing Pattern organization continued to run the processes; accordingly, no T5–T6 gap is documented.
